weapons.name: AMR
weapons.desc: Anti-materiel, and it reads like it. Heavy hits at a pace nothing else at that range can match.

weapons.name: Assault Rifle
weapons.desc: The one everything else is measured against. Nothing it does is remarkable, and there is no fight it cannot hold.

weapons.name: Burst Rifle
weapons.desc: Three rounds a pull, and the gun decides the gap rather than your finger. Slower to the kill than the rifle, and far harder to waste.

weapons.name: Charge Rifle
weapons.desc: Hold it, and it holds. A full charge and three taps ends a standard player (more health takes five taps), which is why it belongs to whoever saw the other person first.
weapons.caution: A full charge spends 10 rounds. With fewer than 10 left a charge fires nothing, and the reload may not take until your next life.

weapons.name: Desert Eagle
weapons.desc: Rounds heavy enough to end a fight your rifle already started, not many of them and slow between pulls. Miss twice and you are reloading in front of someone.

weapons.name: Energy Rifle
weapons.desc: The cell barely stops. When it finally does, the recharge is long enough to lose the fight you were winning.
weapons.caution: Overheats after about 30 rounds of full auto, and it does not cool on its own: work the reload lever to vent the heat (about three pulls, or one held pull), then work the lever to recharge the cell.

weapons.name: Rail Gun
weapons.desc: A single charged slug that ends almost anyone it finds; a full Shields player is left on 1 HP. Two shots, and then it is scrap.

weapons.name: Rocket Launcher
weapons.desc: One round, one player, no argument. Two in the tube and nothing to reload from.

weapons.name: Shotgun
weapons.desc: Three pulls and it is over, if you were close enough to mean it. Shell by shell, and the fastest recovery on the board.

weapons.name: SMG
weapons.desc: A close-combat hose. The barrel hits for 7 and the headset adds 2, so a target reached by both emitters takes 9; the magazine leaves faster than you meant it to.

weapons.name: Sniper Rifle
weapons.desc: One round, then the bolt. Two hits drop anyone from anywhere on the field, and you work the lever between them.

weapons.name: Breacher
weapons.desc: It cannot kill. It takes every layer of armour and shield off whoever you hit, and leaves the finishing to someone else.

weapons.name: Suppressor
weapons.desc: Its own fire sound, and the slowest kill in the game. It is the quiet option for a player who would rather not announce the fight.

weapons.name: Toxin Rifle
weapons.desc: Hits lightly and keeps hitting. The damage arrives after you have stopped shooting, which is the whole point.

weapons.name: USP-S
weapons.desc: A steady sidearm. It will not win a fight you started badly, but it will finish one you nearly had.

perks.name: Body Armor
perks.desc: Start every life with 20 extra armour, about a sixth more total health in Standard. Armour soaks hits before your health does. The rig is heavier though: your reload takes a quarter longer (not the Sniper Rifle's bolt).

perks.name: Extended Mags
perks.desc: In Standard, double the magazine on your primary. In Shields, increase it by 50%. Your reserve grows up to 384 rounds; some rifles already reach that limit. A pistol primary gains 50%, rounded down. The Sniper Rifle is exempt: its bolt keeps one round. The larger magazine slows your weapon swap by 30%.

perks.name: Fast Hands
perks.desc: Reload and swap weapons in half the time. The Sniper Rifle's bolt keeps its normal speed.

perks.name: Armor Piercing
perks.desc: Your primary ignores armor and shields and goes straight to health. The rounds are heavier: fewer of them, and the gun cycles slower. Against a bare target a normal weapon still kills faster, and against an armored or shielded one this wins. It fits any plain-damage primary; the host is told if the chosen weapon cannot carry it.

primary.desc: The one everything else is measured against. Nothing it does is remarkable, and there is no fight it cannot hold.

game.name: Team Deathmatch
game.desc: Squads score a point per elimination. Downed players respawn after the delay and rejoin. First team to the score cap — or the highest score at the time limit — takes the match.
